assessment.title: Azure Networking Assessment
assessment.executive_summary: The Terraform establishes separate application, management, and Private Endpoint subnets, but it does not conform to the required Azure Landing Zone security model. Direct Internet routing bypasses central inspection, RDP is allowed from the Internet, and the workload creates its own hub with incomplete peering instead of consuming a validated platform hub. Storage and Key Vault retain public network access, while Private Endpoint DNS integration is incomplete. Platform-owned firewall, DNS, monitoring, address allocation, and deployed effective-state controls require external validation.

scorecard.summary: A workload-managed hub and one-way peering do not establish approved Landing Zone connectivity.
The application subnet has an explicit default route directly to the Internet.
Internet-sourced RDP and broad intra-VNet defaults conflict with least-privilege controls.
Storage has a Private Endpoint, but Storage and Key Vault remain publicly accessible.
The Private DNS zone is not linked or associated with the Storage Private Endpoint.
No workload diagnostic, flow-log, connectivity-monitoring, or alert resources are declared.

architecture.summary: Terraform declares workload-managed hub and application VNets, three application-side subnets, one-way spoke-to-hub peering, NSGs on application and management subnets, direct Internet egress from the application subnet, and a Storage blob Private Endpoint without complete DNS integration.

flows.name: Storage blob access
flows.status: DNS integration incomplete; public fallback enabled

findings.title: Application egress bypasses central inspection

evidence.detail: The application route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to next hop type Internet.
The bypass route table is associated with the application subnet.

findings.observed_state: Application traffic is explicitly routed directly to the Internet, and no central firewall or approved NVA next hop is referenced.
findings.expected_state: Internet-bound workload traffic must traverse the approved central inspection layer without a direct Internet bypass.
findings.risk: Outbound traffic can evade centrally governed filtering, threat detection, and egress policy.
findings.recommendation: Obtain the approved platform firewall or NVA next-hop details, replace the Internet default route with a VirtualAppliance route, and validate effective routes and return-path symmetry for every workload subnet requiring egress.
dependencies: Platform-provided central inspection next-hop address and routing design

findings.title: Management subnet permits Internet-sourced RDP

evidence.detail: The management NSG allows TCP 3389 from the Internet service tag to any destination.

findings.observed_state: An inbound NSG rule authorizes RDP from the public Internet across the management subnet.
findings.expected_state: Administrative access must use an approved controlled path and administrative ports must not be authorized directly from the Internet without an approved exception.
findings.risk: Any resource later given a viable public ingress path could expose RDP to Internet scanning, credential attacks, and remote compromise.
findings.recommendation: Remove the Internet-sourced RDP rule and implement the approved administrative path, such as Azure Bastion, Entra Private Access, or a restricted private management network with identity-based privileged access controls.

findings.title: Workload recreates an incomplete connectivity hub

evidence.detail: The workload declares and owns a hub VNet rather than referencing an approved platform connectivity resource.
Only application-to-hub peering is declared; no reciprocal hub-to-application peering exists.

findings.observed_state: The repository builds a standalone hub and a single directional peering with no firewall, gateway, DNS, or shared platform integration.
findings.expected_state: The workload must consume the approved centrally managed Landing Zone connectivity platform and establish both directional sides of required VNet peering under the correct ownership model.
findings.risk: The resulting topology can be isolated from enterprise controls and shared services, while incomplete peering can prevent expected hub-initiated or return connectivity.
findings.recommendation: Remove workload ownership of the hub, obtain the approved hub VNet through platform outputs or explicit inputs, retain only the workload-owned peering side, and coordinate the reciprocal platform-owned peering with required forwarded-traffic and gateway settings.

findings.title: Backend PaaS services retain public network paths

evidence.detail: Storage public network access is enabled and network rules use default action Allow.
Key Vault public network access is enabled and no Key Vault Private Endpoint is declared.

findings.observed_state: Storage remains open to public network traffic despite a blob Private Endpoint, and Key Vault has only a public network path.
findings.expected_state: Sensitive backend PaaS services must use approved private connectivity and disable or restrict unrequired public access.
findings.risk: Clients can bypass the intended private path, increasing exposure and weakening network-based data-access controls.
findings.recommendation: Complete and validate private connectivity for required Storage subresources and Key Vault, then disable public network access or apply the explicitly approved restricted-access policy without using public access as a fallback.

findings.title: Storage Private Endpoint lacks usable DNS integration

evidence.detail: A privatelink.blob.core.windows.net zone is created, but no Private DNS zone group or VNet link is declared.

findings.observed_state: The Storage blob Private Endpoint targets the correct subresource and subnet, but Terraform does not register its address in the zone or make the zone resolvable from the application VNet.
findings.expected_state: Private Endpoint names must resolve to the expected private IP through the approved enterprise DNS design, without duplicating centrally owned DNS authority.
findings.risk: Clients can resolve the public endpoint or fail resolution, encouraging continued public access and preventing reliable private connectivity.
findings.recommendation: Confirm Private DNS zone ownership with the platform team; use the shared zone when centrally managed, add the required zone group and approved VNet/DNS resolver integration, and test name resolution separately from TCP connectivity.
dependencies: Enterprise Private DNS zone ownership and resolver design

findings.title: Subnet segmentation does not constrain lateral movement

evidence.detail: Application and management NSGs define no explicit least-privilege east-west rules or denials, leaving default VirtualNetwork access effective.
The Private Endpoint subnet has no NSG association.

findings.observed_state: Subnets are separated by purpose, but their controls do not define or enforce required communication paths between security boundaries.
findings.expected_state: East-west access must be limited to documented application flows and unrelated segments must not receive broad connectivity by default.
findings.risk: Compromise of one segment can enable discovery or access across application, management, and private service boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Document required east-west flows, add least-privilege NSG rules and explicit denials at suitable priorities, associate controls with relevant subnets, and verify both allowed and prohibited paths.

positive_findings.title: Purpose-specific subnet separation
positive_findings.evidence: infra/network.tf separates application, management, and Private Endpoint address ranges.

positive_findings.title: Correct Storage Private Endpoint target
positive_findings.evidence: infra/storage.tf targets the Storage account blob subresource from the dedicated Private Endpoint subnet.

positive_findings.title: Application route table association is explicit
positive_findings.evidence: infra/routing.tf associates the declared route table with the application subnet.

positive_findings.title: PaaS transport baseline is partially hardened
positive_findings.evidence: infra/storage.tf enforces TLS 1.2 and disables anonymous nested-item public access.

assumptions.detail: The platform context states that centrally managed connectivity should be consumed, but no concrete hub, firewall, peering, or routing outputs are available.
assumptions.validation_required: Obtain authoritative platform resource IDs, ownership boundaries, next hops, and peering settings.

assumptions.detail: The 10.10.0.0/16 and 10.20.0.0/16 ranges cannot be compared with enterprise or hybrid networks.
assumptions.validation_required: Confirm both CIDRs against the authoritative IP address management allocation.

assumptions.detail: Private DNS zones and resolver integration may be centrally managed, but no authoritative source identifies ownership.
assumptions.validation_required: Confirm zone ownership, VNet links, resolver paths, and hybrid forwarding with the platform team.

assumptions.detail: The repository contains no diagnostics, flow logs, connectivity monitors, or alert rules; these controls may exist outside the workload repository.
assumptions.validation_required: Verify deployed diagnostic settings, telemetry destinations, retention, critical-path monitoring, and actionable alerts.

assumptions.detail: No authenticated Azure discovery was performed.
assumptions.validation_required: Validate effective routes, peering state, public endpoints, Private Endpoint approval and DNS, NSG effective rules, and possible configuration drift.
